reason: Follow the only available action to start the muscle-cell lineage.
expectation: The signals should guide some stem-cell descendants toward muscle precursors.

effect: The signals produced myoblasts, which are ready to fuse into muscle fibres.
reaction: The label makes the unfamiliar term clear, though the result was expected.
reason: Fusion is the only offered combination and advances the muscle-fibre goal.
expectation: The myoblasts should fuse into a shared, multinucleated muscle fibre.

effect: The fused myoblasts formed multinucleated fibres with space for pulling machinery.
reaction: The retained nuclei make the fusion result clear, as expected.
reason: The only offered combination adds the filaments needed for the fibre to pull.
expectation: The actin and myosin units will be organized inside the fibre, probably preparing it for a calcium-triggered pull.

effect: The fibre now has reset myosin heads, but actin grip sites remain covered; calcium is the next step toward a pull.
reaction: The covered sites make it clear why filaments alone are not enough.
reason: The only offered combination supplies the calcium signal needed to activate the filaments.
expectation: Calcium should expose actin's grip sites so myosin can attach and produce a pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing ATP-driven myosin cycling and filament sliding; the fibre now needs to become ready again.
reaction: The distinction between sliding filaments and shortening filaments is clear and useful.
reason: The only offered combination should remove calcium from around the filaments and prepare the fibre to relax.
expectation: The pumps will use ATP to return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites again so the fibre can relax.

effect: ATP-powered calcium pumping stopped the pull and readied the fibre; the next goal is to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: It is useful that relaxation requires ATP and that an outside pull lengthens the fibre.
reason: The only offered combination adds connective material as a step toward building the muscles.
expectation: The matrix will support or surround the muscle fibres, preparing them for assembly with sheaths and tendons.

effect: The matrix organized the fibres into connective-wrapped fascicles, with enough bundles for both muscles.
reaction: The labelled bundle and distinction between membrane and connective layer clarify the construction.
reason: I'll build the biceps first; both muscles are needed, and either appears to be a reasonable starting point.
expectation: The fascicles should fill the biceps sheaths and connect with its tendons, preparing it for attachment across the elbow.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs building, but I chose to start with the biceps.

effect: The biceps fascicles now connect through sheaths to tendons, ready for attachment to the skeleton.
reaction: The force-tracing inset makes the connective tissue's role clear.
reason: Build the triceps next so both muscles are ready to attach.
expectation: The remaining fascicles should fill the triceps sheaths and connect to its tendons.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the biceps now, but building both muscles first seems straightforward.

effect: Both muscles are now built and ready to attach to the skeleton.
reaction: The triceps construction repeated the biceps force-path inset, but its three heads and ulnar tendon distinguish it.
reason: Attach the biceps first; both muscles need attachment, and either order seems reasonable.
expectation: The biceps tendons should connect across the elbow to the shoulder and radius.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attaching, but I chose to start with the biceps.

effect: The biceps is attached across the elbow and flexes it; the assembly still needs an extensor.
reaction: The two poses clearly connect the biceps tendon’s position to elbow flexion.
reason: The only offered combination fills the extensor slot with the triceps.
expectation: The triceps will attach across the elbow and provide the opposing pull that extends it.

effect: The triceps fills the extensor slot and completes the arm; its posterior attachment turns a pull into elbow extension.
reaction: The paired poses make the opposing actions of the two muscles clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered pull was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects ATP-driven myosin cycling to sliding filaments without implying that the filaments themselves shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps repeated the biceps force-path inset, although the different heads and tendon attachment gave it a purpose.

surprise.text: Relaxation also requires ATP to pump calcium back into storage, and the fibre lengthens under an outside pull.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though most early steps had only one offered combination, so they involved little decision-making. The terms flexor and extensor could be explained more directly for students unfamiliar with anatomy.

continue.text: I would continue: the progression from filament movement to opposing elbow actions made the construction worthwhile, despite some repetitive assembly.
